MUQATIL:11:15-16/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:15-16/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:15-16/r3.claim: Because their deeds were done for worldly gain, they receive only the Fire in the hereafter and their works are void and unaccepted.

TAB-FULL:v12p353#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p353#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p353#2/r1.claim: Those paid for worldly deeds have only the Fire in the afterlife; their work vanishes because they acted for other than God, so He nullifies its reward.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r3.speaker: علي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2010/r3.claim: Ali affirms that the passage describes someone who wants this world and does not want the Hereafter.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2011/r5.claim: Qatada says the world-focused person receives reward for good deeds in this life but reaches the Hereafter with none; a believer receives reward in both lives and is not wronged.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r1.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says that the good deeds polytheists perform in associationism are repaid in this world, leaving them only Hell in the Hereafter.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r2.claim: Al-Suddi glosses حبط as becoming void.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the good works they did were nullified.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the worldly-seeking deeds he performed are nullified and he is among the losers in the Hereafter.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ibn Jurayj, glosses what they did as what they did in this world.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says their deeds are void because they receive no recompense for them in the Hereafter.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2012/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ibn Jurayj, says the phrase refers to their deeds in the world.

THALABI:v5p160#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p160#2/r1.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p160#2/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits that on Judgment Day the first people summoned include a Quran reciter, a wealthy man, and one killed in battle, each questioned about what he did with his gifts.

THALABI:v5p160#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p160#2/r2.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p160#2/r2.claim: The reciter, donor, and fighter are each condemned as seeking fame rather than God; the Prophet says these three are the first fuel for Hell.

THALABI:v5p160#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p160#2/r3.speaker: معاوية
THALABI:v5p160#2/r3.claim: When Shuqayy related Abu Hurayra’s report, Muʿawiya feared what this meant for others, wept, and affirmed the verse about worldly seekers’ ruined deeds.

THALABI:v5p160#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p160#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p160#2/r4.claim: Their apparent good works are ruined in this life and false in what they were doing.

THALABI:v5p160/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p160/r8.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v5p160/r8.claim: Mujahid identifies those whose deeds are void and whose only Hereafter recompense is Fire as usurers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r10.claim: In al-Kalbī's report through Abū Ṣāliḥ, the passage was revealed about people of the qibla.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r11.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r11.claim: The people described are those who act for show.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r5.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's report, those seeking immediate worldly life reject resurrection, reward, and punishment; this makes the passage about unbelievers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r6.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r6.claim: One whose sole concern is worldly life receives recompense for good deeds here, then reaches the afterlife without a good deed to reward; believers are rewarded in both.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r7.claim: Some exegetes apply the verses to unbelievers because of the following verse: believers seek both worlds, with the afterlife their greater aim.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r8.claim: On this reading, an unbeliever's good acts such as feeding, clothing, and defending oppressed Muslims are repaid through worldly prosperity and comforts.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p366/r9.claim: The unbelievers receive their good deeds' reward in this world and have only the Fire in the afterlife, where they regret having no good deed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r1.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r1.claim: A believer who performs a righteous act without God-consciousness is given its reward in this world.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ adopts the view that a person of the qibla who intends worldly reward is paid fully in this life, without any shortfall.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r3.claim: The Prophet describes ostentatious reciters, spenders, and fighters, who acted to earn reputations, as the first people whose Fire is kindled on Judgment Day.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r4.speaker: معاوية
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r4.claim: After hearing the report, Muʿāwiya wept, affirmed that God and His Messenger spoke truth, and recited these two verses.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r5.claim: The warning concerns Muslims whose good acts serve worldly aims without thought of the afterlife; they receive worldly recompense but face punishment if they did not seek God's approval and reward.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r6.claim: Although the wording appears to entail eternal punishment for believers, a believer who dies in faith is not eternally in Hell.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r7.claim: The verse's wording appears to say that ostentation and worldly intent without seeking afterlife reward invalidate faith at death, since “their deeds were null” includes faith and its branches.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p368/r8.claim: People of monotheism do not remain in Hell forever; they are burned for prior sins and then enter Paradise.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:15-17/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:15-17/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:15-17/r4.claim: Such people have only the Fire in the afterlife, and their worldly deeds have become void.

JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r8.claim: Because pursuit of worldly adornment can deter people from religion, those who seek only this life receive the full recompense of their deeds in it, without shortchanging; in the hereafter they have only the Fire and their deeds are null.

JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r9.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v5p3468#2/r9.claim: Al-Aṣamm says the verse concerns polytheists who do good deeds such as maintaining kinship or avoiding injustice without believing in resurrection; their deeds are rejected because they were not done in worship of God, yet they receive their full worldly provision and lifespan.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p166/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p166/r1.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p166/r1.claim: Mujahid says those who seek worldly life with their deeds are people who show off.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p166/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p166/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p166/r2.claim: The Prophet calls showiness the minor shirk he most fears for his community.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p166/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p166/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p166/r3.claim: Another view applies the passage to disbelievers; a believer’s dominant aim is the Hereafter, so good deeds can earn reward in both lives.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p166/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p166/r4.speaker: أنس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p166/r4.claim: Anas reports that God does not wrong a believer’s good deed: the believer receives provision in this life and reward in the next, while a disbeliever’s good deeds are exhausted in this life.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p155#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p155#2/r4.speaker: قتادة والضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p155#2/r4.claim: They take the universal wording about seeking worldly life as specifically referring to disbelievers.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p155#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p155#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p155#2/r5.claim: Mujahid includes disbelievers and believers who act for show; Muawiya adopted this after Shafi ibn Mati al-Asbahi relayed the Prophetic report about a charity-giver, slain fighter, and Qur'an-reciter whose ostentation makes them first fuel for Hell, then wept and cited the passage.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p155#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p155#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p155#2/r6.claim: For the disbeliever reading, يريد means to intend and aim: worldly life is the person's sole goal, without belief in an afterlife; God repays good deeds with worldly favors, though provision may be narrow or ample, and their afterlife is only Fire.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers the disbeliever interpretation because the preceding context concerns those opposing the Qur'an.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r2.claim: On the view that the passage includes sinful believers, يريد means love, prefer, and choose; God rewards good deeds not done for Him with worldly favors, while 'only Fire' means it is what they deserve, though God may forgive them.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r3.claim: Anas says the verses concern the People of the Book; Ibn Atiyya says they are included as disbelievers, not the exclusive referent.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r6.claim: حبط means to become void or fall away, used of corrupted deeds; the Prophet's phrase يقتل حبطا أو يلم illustrates the usage.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r7.claim: The pronoun in فيها first refers to worldly life and in its third occurrence to the afterlife; alternatives make all three refer to this world or the second to deeds.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r8.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r8.claim: The majority read وباطل in the nominative; Ubay and Ibn Masud read وباطلا in the accusative, attested in four codices, with يعملون governing it and ما treated as extra.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p156/r9.claim: باطل is anything whose nature prevents it from attaining a final end such as reward.

TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r3.claim: Such people have only Hell in the hereafter; their deeds are null because they performed them in a way that merits no reward and for other than God.

TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r4.claim: This verifies the author's view that ihbat means nullifying the deed itself when it is done in a manner unworthy of reward.

TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r5.claim: Hasan recounts that a man pursued a girl, struck his face on a wall, recognized it as punishment for his sin, and told the Prophet.

TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله
TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r6.claim: The Prophet tells him God hastened punishment for his sin in this life: if God intends good, He punishes a servant here; if evil, He withholds punishment until the Day of Resurrection.

TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:15-16#2/r7.claim: The connection answers whether outwardly professing Islam for worldly safety suffices: worldly seeking, by profession or other means, leads to this outcome.

TABRISI:11:15-16/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16/r1.speaker: أبي، ابن مسعود
TABRISI:11:15-16/r1.claim: Anomalous readings attributed to Ubayy and Ibn Masud have وباطلا ما كانوا يعملون.

TABRISI:11:15-16/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:15-16/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:15-16/r2.claim: On that reading, باطلا is an accusative governed by يعملون, and ما is an emphatic extra particle, as in the cited Qur'anic construction.

RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r1.claim: The opponents claimed to dispute with Muhammad to establish truth, but Rāzī says envy and refusal to follow him were their real motives.

RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r2.claim: The verse resembles 17:18 and 42:20, which distinguish those seeking worldly life from those seeking the harvest of the hereafter.

RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r3.claim: One view restricts the verse to disbelievers because its ending about hell and nullified deeds cannot describe believers generally; the general opening is narrowed to those seeking only worldly adornment.

RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r4.speaker: الأصم
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r4.claim: Al-Aṣamm says the disbelievers who deny resurrection are intended, since they desire only worldly happiness.

RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r5.claim: Another view identifies hypocrites who joined the Prophet's campaigns to seek spoils without belief in afterlife reward.

RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r6.speaker: أنس
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r6.claim: A third view, transmitted from Anas, identifies Jews and Christians.

RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r7.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v17p158#2/r7.claim: The Qāḍī's chosen reading concerns people who do good deeds for worldly praise: social benefits such as charity and public works benefit others, but worship without proper intention is not obedience.

RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r1.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r1.claim: On the Qāḍī's view, the deeds meant are good works that a disbeliever can validly perform.

RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r2.claim: A second view takes the wording generally, including believers who act for reputation and disbelievers who seek worldly reward; the hell clause is difficult unless it means punishment for those corrupted acts.

RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r3.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits a prophetic report that the Qurʾān reciter, wealthy donor, and martyr are condemned because each sought public praise rather than God.

RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v17p159/r4.claim: After Abū Hurayra recited this report to Muʿāwiya, the narrator says Muʿāwiya wept and then affirmed the truth of the verse.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:16/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:16/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:16/r1.claim: The warning indicates eternal punishment; since believers do not remain eternally in Hell (4:116), it applies when the hypocrite dies in disbelief.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:16/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:16/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:11:16/r2.claim: An alternative says they enter Hell for a specified number of days, then leave through intercession or a divine release.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:16/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:16/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:16/r3.claim: The verse threatens loss of faith, especially through ostentation, which is a form of shirk as explained under al-Nisa and later under al-Kahf.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:16/r4.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:11:16/r4.claim: Abu Hatim treats the wording as involving an omitted pronoun; al-Nahhas says no deletion is needed because باطل is verbal-noun usage, meaning their work is void.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:16/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:16/r5.speaker: أبي وعبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:11:16/r5.claim: Ubayy and Abdullah read وباطلا ما كانوا يعملون, taking ما as extra and the sense as they practiced falsehood.

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:16-17/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:16-17/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:16-17/r1.claim: Those seeking only the world have only Fire in the afterlife; their deeds yield no reward because they lacked sincerity, were not rightly performed, or were confined to worldly aims.

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:16-17/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:16-17/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:16-17/r2.claim: The two statements explain the preceding threat: their work has no afterlife reward, and what they did was itself invalid; one reading makes batilan the object of ya'malun.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p149#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p149#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p149#2/r1.claim: Such people have only the Fire in the afterlife; their work earns no reward there because they intended this world and received what they sought.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p149#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p149#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p149#2/r2.claim: Their deeds are intrinsically futile because they were done without a proper purpose; work with no valid aim merits no reward.

QASHANI:11:16-17/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:16-17/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:16-17/r1.claim: Such people face the afterlife's fire because worldly veils frustrate the heart's aptitude and cause distress from ill-fitting acquisitions; their outwardly good deeds vanish because they intended worldly gain.

QASHANI:11:16-17/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:16-17/r2.speaker: عليه السلام
QASHANI:11:16-17/r2.claim: A prophetic report that actions are judged by intentions supports the nullification of deeds performed for worldly ends.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r4.claim: Restricting the Fire to these people most clearly indicates unbelievers; if ostentatious believers are included, it means the Fire is their due, though God may forgive them, as Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Jubayr apparently hold.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r5.claim: The pronoun in ما صنعوا فيها apparently refers to the afterlife, where deeds come to nothing, but it may refer to worldly life; ما may be relative or a verbal noun.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r6.claim: باطل reinforces the stated nullification; it may begin a new clause or be a second predicate, with corresponding analyses of ما كانوا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r7.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p132/r7.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAli reads وبطل as a past verb; Ubayy and Ibn Masʿud read وباطلا in the accusative, parsed as an object of يعملون with ما extra, though the syntax is disputed.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p134/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p134/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p134/r1.claim: Invalid deeds deserve no reward because they were not done with a sound intention.

SAMIN-DURR:11:16#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:16#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:16#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari's emphatic ما analysis is illustrated with poetry: وحديث ما على قصره and لأمر ما جدع قصير أنفه.

SAMIN-DURR:11:16#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:16#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:16#2/r2.claim: The same use of ما had been discussed under the expression مثلا ما بعوضة, cited here as الزمر 39:9.

SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r1.claim: In وحبط ما صنعوا فيها, فيها may modify حبط and refer to the afterlife, or modify صنعوا and refer to worldly life as in 11:15.

SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r2.claim: ما صنعوا may be a relative pronoun with an omitted object pronoun, or a verbal noun meaning their making has perished.

SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r3.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r3.claim: The majority read باطل in the nominative; one analysis makes it a fronted predicate and ما كانوا يعملون its subject, with ما either relative or verbal noun.

SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r4.speaker: مكي بن أبي طالب
SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r4.claim: Makki makes باطل the subject and ما كانوا يعملون the predicate; the author says this is possible only as an error and criticizes Makki for giving no other analysis.

SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r5.claim: A third nominative parse coordinates باطل with the preceding predicates, taking ما كانوا يعملون as its subject; Zayd ibn Ali's verbal reading supports it.

SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r6.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads وباطل as a past-tense verb coordinated with حبط.

SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r7.speaker: أبي وابن مسعود
SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r7.claim: Ubayy and Ibn Masud read باطلا in the accusative; Makki says this is also how it appears in their codices.

SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r8.speaker: مكي وأبو البقاء وصاحب اللوامح
SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r8.claim: They take accusative باطلا as the object of يعملون with an extra ما, allowing the predicate of كان to precede it.

SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:11:16/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows ما to be emphatic and Baṭilan to mean utterly false, or باطلا to be a verbal noun.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says ostentatious people receive in this world the reward for good deeds done solely for worldly gain, such as fasting, prayer, or night vigil, but their work is void in the Hereafter; Mujahid and al-Dahhak also report this view.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r2.claim: Anas and Hasan say these verses were revealed about Jews and Christians.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r3.claim: Mujahid and others identify the people addressed as those who act for show.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p310#2/r4.claim: Qatada says those whose goal and intention are worldly receive their good deeds' reward here, then arrive with no rewarded good deed; believers are rewarded both here and in the Hereafter.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p512/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p512/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p512/r1.claim: Those people receive only Fire in the afterlife after taking their full reward in this world; their works collapse because they lack a sound foundation and are empty forms.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p512/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p512/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p512/r2.claim: The author defines adornment as beautification by clothing, jewelry, or appearance; full recompense as delivering a right completely; and the nullification of work through the image of a spoiled stomach.

DURR-FULL:v4p405/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p405/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن معبد
DURR-FULL:v4p405/r7.claim: In response to a question to Ali, the verse concerns a person who wants worldly life and seeks no Hereafter.

DURR-FULL:v4p405/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p405/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p405/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the desired life as its reward and adornment as its wealth; God fully grants health, family joy, money, and children, a rule he says was abrogated by 17:18.

DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r1.claim: The Prophet describes three groups among his community: sincere worshippers enter Paradise, while those who worship for worldly gain or to be seen are sent to Hell.

DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says hypocritical people will see Paradise's scent and palaces, then be denied its reward and taste painful punishment because they performed before people but disregarded God in private.

DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r3.claim: The worldly seeker receives the reward of his deed here but nothing in the Hereafter; Sa'id compares this to the verse about usury not growing with God.

DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r4.claim: Qatada says whoever makes worldly life his sole concern is repaid good deeds here but has no good in the Hereafter; a believer may be rewarded in both worlds, without being wronged.

DURR-FULL:v4p407/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p407/r1.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v4p407/r1.claim: Al-Suddi gives the same interpretation that worldly seekers receive what they seek in this life.

DURR-FULL:v4p407/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p407/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p407/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says even prayer, fasting, and night worship can be done to obtain worldly benefit; its seeker receives that benefit, but the deed is null and he loses in the Hereafter.

DURR-FULL:v4p407/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p407/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p407/r6.claim: The Prophet says the first judged include a Qur'an reciter, a wealthy donor, and a slain fighter; each is condemned because he acted for public praise and is sent to Hell. Al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan.

DURR-FULL:v4p408/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p408/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p408/r1.claim: Mujahid says one who works for worldly gain without seeking God receives the full recompense for that work in this life.

DURR-FULL:v4p408/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p408/r2.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
DURR-FULL:v4p408/r2.claim: A person's standing with God is reflected in their deeds; the believer may be rewarded in both worlds, while the unbeliever receives worldly reward only.

DURR-FULL:v4p408/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p408/r6.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v4p408/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says their good deeds are annulled and they receive no recompense in the Hereafter.

DURR-FULL:v4p408/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p408/r8.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v4p408/r8.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b is reported to recite “and void were the deeds they used to do.”

ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#2/r1.claim: The demonstrative may refer to persistent worldly intent, full recompense in this life, or both; its distance signals how far the people are from goodness.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#2/r2.claim: They have only Hell in the afterlife because their aims and actions were confined to worldly acquisition, whose reward they already received.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#2/r3.claim: On the apparent reading, their deeds are shown to have come to nothing in the afterlife; ما may be a verbal noun or refer to the deeds that could have earned afterlife reward.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, فيها can refer to worldly life, describing the failure of their works through lack of sincerity or their having been rewarded in this world.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#3/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#3/r1.claim: Abū Ḥayyān takes the final sentence as emphasis of the preceding claim that their works came to nothing.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#3/r2.speaker: أبو السعود
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#3/r2.claim: Abū al-Suʿūd distinguishes their outwardly good works, which fail to earn reward for lack of faith or right intention, from worldly pursuits intrinsically without lasting benefit; al-Ālūsī prefers this account.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#3/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī offers, but regards as unlikely, reading ما كانوا يعملون as their continuing desire for worldly life itself, a work of the heart.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#3/r4.claim: The normal syntax makes باطل a fronted predicate and ما كانوا يعملون its subject; other grammatical parses and the verbal reading بطل are also reported.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#3/r5.speaker: أبي وابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v12p24#3/r5.claim: Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd read باطلا in the accusative, with several possible grammatical explanations for the construction.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p25/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p25/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p25/r1.claim: The verse applies generally to unbelievers whose good works lack the orientation required for afterlife reward; Jews and Christians may be occasions of revelation without being its exclusive subject.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p25/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p25/r2.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v12p25/r2.claim: A report from Anas says the verse was revealed about Jews and Christians; Ibn ʿAṭiyya treats them as a cause of revelation included within a general rule.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p25/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p25/r3.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p25/r3.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī applies the verse to hypocrites who fought with the Prophet and received booty, but al-Ālūsī objects that the Meccan verse preceded that event.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p25/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p25/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p25/r4.claim: Some apply the verse to ostentatious worshippers, citing the report that a reciter, giver, or fallen fighter seeking reputation is told that he has received it but no divine reward; Muʿāwiya wept at the citation.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p25/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p25/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p25/r5.claim: Unbelievers commonly receive worldly recompense through health, wealth, and children; some scholars say good deeds lessen their afterlife punishment, while others deny benefit where intention is a condition, reconciling the evidence this way.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p26/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p26/r1.speaker: مجمع البيان
ALUSI-FULL:v12p26/r1.claim: Majmaʿ al-Bayān connects the passage to the earlier question Will you submit?: if people profess Islam to protect life and property, this verse explains the result.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p26/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p26/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p26/r2.claim: Another proposed link is that unbelievers might profess Islam or do good works in hopes of protection after hearing that their idols cannot save them; al-Ālūsī notes the account assumes such a precautionary intent.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p26/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p26/r3.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v12p26/r3.claim: Al-Baḥr relates the verse to the preceding discussion by adding the unbelievers' worldly circumstances and their ultimate afterlife outcome.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p26/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p26/r4.speaker: أبو السعود
ALUSI-FULL:v12p26/r4.claim: Abū al-Suʿūd says the passage addresses unbelievers generally, especially Quranic critics: their apparent worldly gains do not show that they possess truth or anything substantial.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p26/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p26/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p26/r5.claim: The verse is cited against charging for acts whose proper purpose is devotion; al-Kiyā al-Ṭabarī also invokes it for intention-dependent fasting and ablution, a disputed legal inference.

ELMALILI:11:16/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:16/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:16/r1.claim: Those described as seeking worldly life and its adornment will have only the Fire in the hereafter.

ELMALILI:11:16/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:16/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:16/r2.claim: Any good they did in this world is nullified in the hereafter because their intentions were not good and all their work served worldly life alone.

ELMALILI:11:16/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:16/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:16/r3.claim: Every effort to preserve or adorn the transient world is empty because death erases it all; any deed not done purely for God is void, since everything besides God perishes.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p22/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p22/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p22/r1.claim: This parenthetical warning follows the challenge to submit: if people seek worldly rank instead of truth, their worldly enjoyment ends in lasting punishment; the second clause is the main point.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p22/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p22/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p22/r2.claim: The warning explains resistance to faith and cautions Muslims not to mistake unbelievers' worldly ease for divine approval or assume disbelief brings immediate punishment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p23/r1.claim: The Prophet renounced much luxury and adornment, framing the women choice as a question of lifestyle.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r3.claim: The next sentence is independent but linked by “those”; the demonstrative marks the people and signals that their prior traits justify the judgment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r4.claim: The exception means that nothing in the afterlife is theirs except the Fire, which entails eternal punishment and identifies them as unbelievers.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r5.claim: Hābiṭ means becoming void or annihilated.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r6.claim: “What they made” means their deeds, including worldly kindness such as feeding the needy; ṣanīʿa names a benevolent deed, fitting the wording.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r7.claim: “In it” may refer to this world, modifying their deeds, or the afterlife, where their deeds have no effect; their share of divine favor is confined to worldly life.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p24/r8.claim: The Prophet told Umar that Persians and Romans had received their good things early in worldly life.

TABATABAI:11:15-16/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:15-16/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:15-16/r5.claim: Because they did not intend an afterlife goal, these people have only Hell there; their deeds are erased and rendered void, like wood consumed by fire.

TABATABAI:11:16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:16/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:16/r1.claim: The two clauses about deeds being erased and made void explain what it means to have only the Fire in the afterlife; another passage calls Hell the abode of ruin.

ASAD-NOTES:11:15#n27/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:15#n27/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:15#n27/r1.claim: Good deeds are fully counted on Judgment Day but outweighed by disbelief in resurrection and the life to come.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Quraysh argued that the Prophet’s and his companions’ poverty disproved prophethood, while their own wealth suggested God favored them rather than threatened them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Worldly pleasures are not rewards for good deeds; God gives them to both virtuous people and wrongdoers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Actions focused wholly on this world are baseless even when an undertaking appears pious.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Hereafter-directed effort counts only when done with faith, sincerity, and fitting righteous action; ostentation, shirk, and verbal claims to Paradise have no value.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:15/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:15/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:15/r1.claim: God does not leave anyone’s work unrewarded: people receive returns in the fields where they develop their God-given abilities, as 3:145 also says.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:15/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:15/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:15/r2.claim: Those who disbelieve in the afterlife and use their abilities only for worldly pleasure, security, wealth, influence, and display receive their full return in this life, but their only afterlife outcome is Hell.

STUDYQURAN:11:15/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:15/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:15/r4.claim: The nullification of actions performed with wrong intentions in the Hereafter is also discussed at 3:22.

STUDYQURAN:11:15/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:15/r5.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:11:15/r5.claim: Some invoke the hadith that actions are judged according to intentions in explaining the fate of deeds.
